title: WPMS/1699/2015 of Reinforced Earth India Pvt Ltd Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION (M/S) No. 1699 of 2015
Reinforced Earth India Pvt. Ltd.
 ..... Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and another ... Respondents
Present :
Mr. Gurinder Pal Singh, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. A.K. Joshi, Addl. C.S.C. for the State/respondents.
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J. (Oral)
 Present petition is filed seeking writ of
certiorari quashing the tender condition Sr. No. 5,
whereby bids were invited from different contractors to
supply and laying of high strength geogrids, having
planar structure consisting of a monoaxial array of
composite geosynthetics strips. Each single longitudinal
strip has a core of high tenacity polyester yarns tendons
encased in a polyethylene sheath; the single strips are
connected by non resisting cross laid polyethylene strip,
which gives a grid like shape to the composite. (Material
should conform to detailed specifications and drawings
as attached. MORTH specification Section No. 3100 (As
per drawing No. DWG/R1/04); further writ of
mandamus commanding the respondents to re-design
the tender documents by including supply and laying of
high strength polyester geogrid coated with bitumen,
polyester geogrid coated with PVC, HDPL geogrid and to
include geostrip or geostrap, which may constitute
geogrid.
 Mr. Gurinder Pal Singh, learned counsel
appearing for the petitioner, has vehemently argued that
geogrid polyethylene sheath is manufactured by only
one company based in Italy i.e. M/s Maccaferri. Further

2
contends that tender notice was so designed with
ulterior motive so that only one manufacturer i.e. Italian
Company M/s Maccaferri may participate in the tender
process. Mr. Gurinder Pal Singh further contends that in
case polyethylene geostraps or geostrips are put together
they may constitute geodgrids and will give more
strength than geogrids of polyethylene. Further
contended that even Government of India has approved
geogrid polyethylene sheath as well as polyester geogrid
coated with Bitumen polyester geogrid coated with PVC
as well as geostrip and geostrap, therefore, respondents
ought to have invited geostrip and geostrap as well,
which are akin to geogrid of polyethylene if placed
together.
 On being asked, Mr. Gurinder Pal Singh,
learned counsel for the petitioner, submits that there is
no dispute to the fact that M/s Meccaferri, the Italian
Company, is only a manufacturer of polyethylene
geogrid and does not undertake civil contract work.
 Careful reading of tender notice would reveal
that respondents have not invited bids from the
manufacturer of the polyethylene geogrid. Rather they
have invited bids from the contractors who have
experience of similar type of work.
 In view of the above, in my humble opinion,
there may be many contractors who are having similar
experience to lay down the polyethylene geogrids to
avoid less ride and it would be their headache to take
supply of polyethylene geogrids after having negotiation
with the manufacturer of that product.
 There is another aspect of the matter i.e. as to
whether polyethylene geogrid would be more
appropriate in a civil contract in question or geostrip

3
and geostrap of polyethylene can be used, can be
decided only by the technocrats and experts of the field.
This Court while exercising writ jurisdiction under
Article 226 of the Constitution of India is not supposed
to act as an expert of the field to say that
geostrap/geostrip if put together would also give the
more strength than the polyethylene geogrid.
 Secondly, calling the bid from the contractors
who have experience of similar type of works cannot be
said to be arbitrary.
 In view of the above, I am not inclined to
entertain this petition. Consequently, petition fails and
is hereby dismissed.
 CLMA No. 7824 of 2015 also stands disposed
of accordingly.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
Dated: 13th July, 2015
Avneet/
